transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (PulseMed CTO), Ben Ortiz (PulseMed ML Eng), Sara Lee (PulseMed Infra)
Recording link: https://redwood-share.example.com/recording/ff-20261103 (note: link placeholder)

Auto-generated Summary: Weekly benchmark review vs baseline provider. Discussed p50/p95, batching, KV cache, quantization impacts, deployment options and next steps. Action items captured.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about an hour. Marco's going to walk through the updated benchmark sheet, and then we'll go over the customer metrics and next steps. Aisha, Ben, Sara, are we good on time?
[00:08] Aisha (CTO): Yep good here, go ahead.
[00:12] Marco (SE): Cool. Quick context, we re-ran the baseline vs Redwood Dedicated with batching and KV cache on. The test workload is the 7b-ish model you requested - it's a trimmed-down paraphrase model, 512 token average context, we did both cold and warm cache runs. The sheet is in the shared drive -- link in chat.
[00:30] Ben (ML Eng): I saw the preliminary numbers, p50 looked great but p95 looks... higher than we expected. Can you explain the variance?
[00:40] Marco (SE): Yeah so p50 with KV cache warm and 8-way batching is around 80ms on H100-equivalent; p95 is about 380ms in our runs, p99 at ~620ms. The baseline provider had p50 ~120ms, p95 ~520ms. So we're lower across the board but you can see the tail is influenced by sequence length skew and occasional cold-cache misses.
[01:02] Ben: Right, we have a long-tail of longer prompts in prod which inflates tail latency. We also saw some jitter in the baseline data, just want to be sure the comparison apples-to-apples.
[01:12] Marco: Totally. For apples-to-apples we aligned the prompt distribution and used identical model checkpoints; the main diffs are kernel selection and quantization strategy. We used int8 with a symmetric quant profile that preserves logits well, but for longer sequences we saw extra kernel swaps that add ~50-80ms occasionally.
[01:30] Sara (Infra): Which GPU did you run on? We run A100s in our cluster.
[01:34] Marco: These runs were on H100-like hardware in our Dedicated lab. We also queued an A100 run to mirror yours - early numbers show +20-25% latency on A100 vs H100 for the same config. We'll send the exact numbers.
[01:48] Aisha: Curious about cost. Baseline provider is pushing lower per-token cost but with higher latency; our SLAs care about p95 under 500ms.
[01:56] Lena: This is the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. Redwood can route sensitive traffic to Dedicated pools for p95 guarantees and route bulk workloads to hosted cheaper variants. For the POC we can show cost modelling.
[02:12] Ben: Can you quantify the batching impact? If we bump batch size more aggressively, does that change tail behavior?
[02:18] Marco: Batching improves throughput and unit cost, but increases queuing latency for single-call requests. Our 8-way batching hit was chosen as a middle ground. For your 99th percentile, micro-batches plus KV cache warm gives the best tail because cached prefixes avoid repeated work.
[02:36] Ben: What's the KV cache hit rate you observed?
[02:39] Marco: On the warm-run scenario we had ~67% prefix hit rate for your synthetic trace. That reduced end-to-end token generation by roughly 40% on average - big cost savings. But if your production has fewer prefix overlaps, savings will be smaller.
[02:54] Aisha: Our real traffic has some repeat patterns for chart summaries and discharge notes, so I expect decent hits, maybe 50-60%. We'll share a sample.
[03:02] Lena: Great. Ben, Sara, if you can send a request histogram (latency by prompt length) that would help Marco tune the kernel selection and batching policy.
[03:12] Ben: I'll export that today.
[03:15] Sara: I'll try to spin up a test VPC peering so you can run the private deploy pilot - are there any network requirements?
[03:22] Marco: We need to allow egress to the Redwood control plane for metrics, and a peered VPC for model traffic. We'll send the exact CIDR and ports in the infra doc.
[03:33] Aisha: On security, we need SOC2 and KMS details before we hand over PHI data.
[03:39] Lena: Understood - I'll send the security pack: SOC2 report, ISO blurb, KMS/HSM integration notes, audit log examples. We also support customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
[03:49] Ben: Back to numbers - can you share the raw CSV with per-request latencies? The aggregate p95 is fine but we want to see distribution.
[03:57] Marco: Yep will share the CSV. Note some of those entries include transcription noise - I mean, kernel-level artifacts - but we'll annotate.
[04:07] Aisha: You mentioned quantization. Is int8 safe for our quality thresholds? We measure ROUGE/accuracy on our eval set.
[04:14] Marco: For the model family you're using, int8 regressed <0.5% on your evals in our runs. We can test int8+ptq vs int8+awq and also a float16 baseline. If quality drift is a concern we can fallback to fp16 on canary traffic.
[04:30] Ben: Any plans to test dynamic quantization or per-channel scales?
[04:35] Marco: We experimented with per-channel for attention kernels which improves LL by small margins but sometimes increases latency due to extra ops; it's on our tuning list.
[04:44] Sara: About the baseline provider - their profile shows consistent cold-start overheads, is that something Redwood can guarantee to avoid?
[04:51] Lena: Redwood's Dedicated pools keep warmed workers and maintain KV in memory for pinned models, so cold starts are minimal. There are still occasional GC or kernel reload events but far less frequent.
[05:03] Ben: Did you measure throughput (RPS) at target concurrency?
[05:07] Marco: Yes, with a 4x instance Dedicated pool we sustained ~220 RPS with 8-way batching on H100, average latency p50 80ms, p95 380ms. Baseline did ~170 RPS with higher tail. We'll share the throughput curves.
[05:25] Aisha: For our SLOs, p95 under 500ms is acceptable - looks like Redwood meets that if KV hits are decent. What's the margin for error?
[05:34] Marco: With current config we have ~20% headroom for spike traffic; if you need stronger guarantees we recommend reserved capacity (Dedicated commits) sized to your 95th percentile.
[05:46] Lena: Also note routing policies - we can do overflow to cheaper hosted variants for non-critical flows, that helps cost during bursts.
[05:56] Ben: Any known regression risk from model updates? We run frequent model rollouts.
[06:00] Marco: We have rollout tools with canary split and automatic fallbacks. We also integrate eval sets and prompt-based regressions; Redwood Optimize can notify when quality drops.
[06:12] Aisha: Sounds good. Let's define next steps and owners.
[06:16] Lena: OK action item recap: Marco will run the 1k warm KV + batching run and add H100 vs A100 comparison. Ben will send request histogram and sample prompts. Sara will set up VPC. I'll send security docs and pricing today. We'll meet next week same time.
[06:32] Ben: Quick question about pricing - Dedicated monthly commit vs on-demand, do you have a ballpark?
[06:36] Lena: I'll push the sheet, but typical committed pool pricing for a mid-size dedicated cluster starts X - I'll put concrete numbers in the sheet and include a modeled TCO vs baseline provider.
[06:48] Aisha: If we see similar latency and 10-15% cost delta in your favor, we can move to a pilot Dedicated for a 30-day run.
[06:55] Lena: Great. Anything else?
[06:57] Sara: No, that's it from infra.
[06:59] Marco: One more note - we'll include logs showing KV eviction patterns. That should help you tune TTL and prefix hashing.
[07:06] Ben: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:09] Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the sheet and the runs. Bye.

End of transcript.

Artifacts referenced: Benchmark spreadsheet (GDrive link placeholder), Security pack (SOC2 + KMS PDF), sample traces (to be provided by customer).
